Looking at the folds: the diamond-shaped square is first folded along the vertical diagonal, then along the horizontal line, giving a small right triangle whose vertical leg is the first crease, horizontal leg is the second crease, and hypotenuse is the outer edge.

The cut removes the top corner (the original top vertex of the square) with a horizontal cut perpendicular to the vertical crease.

- Unfolding the second fold (horizontal crease) mirrors the cut to the bottom corner as well.
- Unfolding the first fold (vertical crease) mirrors each cut across the vertical diagonal, completing full horizontal cuts across the top and bottom corners.

So the unfolded square has its top and bottom corners sliced off by straight horizontal lines, leaving a hexagon with flat horizontal top and bottom edges and pointed left and right corners — exactly shape E.

\boxed{E}
